148: // guardedConfigureClient composes a client's optional pre-existing
149: // ConfigureClient hook with the dial-time SSRF guard. It is installed on a
150: // *fasthttp.Client as the bound method value (&guardedConfigureClient{…}).run,
151: // which fasthttp calls once per HostClient it creates — so the guard is
152: // present before the first dial to each host and covers both the Dial and
153: // DialTimeout code paths.
154: //
155: // The bound method's code pointer is stable across receivers (unlike a
156: // closure's), so ensureClientGuarded recognizes an already-guarded client by
157: // identity — no package-level map keyed by the client, which would pin the
158: // client and its connection pool for the process lifetime. The struct is
159: // referenced only from the client's own ConfigureClient field, so it is
160: // collected together with the client.
161: type guardedConfigureClient struct {
162: 	// orig is the caller's ConfigureClient hook, or nil. It runs before the
163: 	// guard so the guard wraps whatever Dial/DialTimeout it finally sets —
164: 	// running it after would let a hook that assigns hc.Dial overwrite the
165: 	// guard and reopen the SSRF hole.
166: 	orig func(hc *fasthttp.HostClient) error
167: }
168: 
169: func (g *guardedConfigureClient) run(hc *fasthttp.HostClient) error {
170: 	if g.orig != nil {
171: 		if err := g.orig(hc); err != nil {
172: 			return err
173: 		}
174: 	}
175: 	installHostClientGuard(hc)
176: 	return nil
177: }

179: // guardHookPtr is the code pointer shared by every guardedConfigureClient.run
180: // method value, used to detect whether a client is already guarded.
181: var guardHookPtr = reflect.ValueOf((&guardedConfigureClient{}).run).Pointer()
182: 
183: // guardMu serializes the read-modify-write of a client's ConfigureClient in
184: // ensureClientGuarded, so a concurrent guarder cannot write the field mid
185: // update or observe it half-installed.
186: var guardMu sync.Mutex
187: 
188: // ensureClientGuarded installs the SSRF guard on cli via its ConfigureClient
189: // hook, exactly once (idempotent: a client already carrying the guard method
190: // is left untouched). It composes with any hook the client already has,
191: // without retaining a reference to the client. It is invoked at registration
192: // for the default client (init) and WithClient clients — before either is
193: // used — and on the dispatch path only for a per-call variadic client (the
194: // global client is already guarded), so the common no-variadic request path
195: // never reaches this lock. A handler built with a fixed variadic client (e.g.
196: // Forward(addr, cli)) does take guardMu once per request; that is a deliberate
197: // correctness-over-throughput choice (an unlocked fast path would race a
198: // first-time writer).
199: //
200: // Guarantee scope: the default client and WithClient clients are fully
201: // protected. A client supplied as a per-call variadic argument is guarded on
202: // first use — but a host it had already dialed keeps its cached, pre-hook
203: // HostClient, and mutating a client shared with concurrent non-proxy use is
204: // inherently racy. For a full guarantee with a custom client, register it
205: // via WithClient before first use, or hand the proxy a dedicated client.
206: func ensureClientGuarded(cli *fasthttp.Client) {
207: 	guardMu.Lock()
208: 	defer guardMu.Unlock()
209: 
210: 	existing := cli.ConfigureClient
211: 	if existing != nil && reflect.ValueOf(existing).Pointer() == guardHookPtr {
212: 		return // already guarded (directly or composed with a user hook)
213: 	}
214: 	cli.ConfigureClient = (&guardedConfigureClient{orig: existing}).run
215: }

219: 	client.Store(defaultClient)

222: // WithClient sets the global proxy client.
223: // This function should be called before Do and Forward — doing so installs
224: // the dial-time SSRF guard (via the client's ConfigureClient hook,
225: // composing with any hook it already carries) before the client dials any
226: // host, so requests dispatched through it re-validate the resolved IP at
227: // connect time, matching the default client's behavior.
228: func WithClient(cli *fasthttp.Client) {
229: 	if cli == nil {
230: 		panic("proxy: WithClient requires a non-nil *fasthttp.Client")
231: 	}

233: 	ensureClientGuarded(cli)
234: 	client.Store(cli)

237: // Forward performs the given http request and fills the given http response.
238: // This method will return a fiber.Handler
239: //
240: // SSRF note: Forward validates the upstream host against the active
241: // SecurityPolicy up front and, when AllowPrivateIPs is false, re-validates
242: // the resolved IP at dial time via the guard installed on the dispatching
243: // client, so a rebinding-capable resolver cannot swap a public answer for
244: // a private one between validation and connection.
245: func Forward(addr string, clients ...*fasthttp.Client) fiber.Handler {
246: 	return func(c fiber.Ctx) error {
247: 		c.Request().Header.Set("X-Real-IP", c.IP())
248: 		return Do(c, addr, clients...)
249: 	}
250: }

252: // Do performs the given http request and fills the given http response.
253: // This method can be used within a fiber.Handler
254: //
255: // SSRF note: the upstream host is validated against the active
256: // SecurityPolicy before the request is sent, and when AllowPrivateIPs is
257: // false the resolved IP is re-validated at dial time by the guard
258: // installed on the dispatching *fasthttp.Client. The connection therefore
259: // targets exactly the address that passed the blocklist, so a
260: // rebinding-capable resolver cannot slip a private IP past the check.
261: //
262: // The guard is installed via the client's ConfigureClient hook, which only
263: // affects HostClients created after installation. The default client and
264: // WithClient clients are guarded before first use; a client supplied as a
265: // per-call variadic override is guarded on first use, so a host it had
266: // already dialed keeps a cached, pre-guard HostClient. For a full guarantee
267: // with a custom client, register it via WithClient (or pass a dedicated,
268: // unused client) before first use.
269: func Do(c fiber.Ctx, addr string, clients ...*fasthttp.Client) error {
270: 	return doAction(c, addr, func(cli *fasthttp.Client, req *fasthttp.Request, resp *fasthttp.Response, _ *url.URL) error {
271: 		return cli.Do(req, resp)
272: 	}, clients...)
273: }

275: // DoRedirects performs the given http request and fills the given http response, following up to maxRedirectsCount redirects.
276: // When the redirect count exceeds maxRedirectsCount, ErrTooManyRedirects is returned.
277: // This method can be used within a fiber.Handler
278: //
279: // Each redirect target is re-validated against the active SecurityPolicy.
280: // Unless AllowHTTPSDowngrade is enabled, redirects from an HTTPS origin
281: // to a plaintext HTTP target are rejected with ErrRedirectDowngrade.
282: //
283: // SSRF note: every hop's host is validated against the policy, and when
284: // AllowPrivateIPs is false each dial is re-validated by the guard on the
285: // dispatching client — so per-hop redirects (including cross-host ones)
286: // cannot be rebound to a private IP between validation and connection.
287: func DoRedirects(c fiber.Ctx, addr string, maxRedirectsCount int, clients ...*fasthttp.Client) error {
288: 	policy := currentSecurityPolicy()
289: 	return doActionWithPolicy(c, addr, policy, func(cli *fasthttp.Client, req *fasthttp.Request, resp *fasthttp.Response, u *url.URL) error {
290: 		return followRedirects(cli, req, resp, maxRedirectsCount, u, policy)
291: 	}, clients...)

310: func DoTimeout(c fiber.Ctx, addr string, timeout time.Duration, clients ...*fasthttp.Client) error {
311: 	return doAction(c, addr, func(cli *fasthttp.Client, req *fasthttp.Request, resp *fasthttp.Response, _ *url.URL) error {
312: 		return cli.DoTimeout(req, resp, timeout)
313: 	}, clients...)

317: // Receivers are handed the validated *url.URL alongside the request so
318: // they can avoid re-parsing or re-validating the upstream addr.
319: type doActionFunc func(cli *fasthttp.Client, req *fasthttp.Request, resp *fasthttp.Response, u *url.URL) error

323: 	addr string,

330: func doActionWithPolicy(
331: 	c fiber.Ctx,
332: 	addr string,
333: 	policy SecurityPolicy,
334: 	action doActionFunc,
335: 	clients ...*fasthttp.Client,
336: ) error {
337: 	globalClient := client.Load()
338: 
339: 	cli, err := selectClient(globalClient, clients...)
340: 	if err != nil {
341: 		return err
342: 	}
343: 
344: 	// The global client (default or WithClient) is guarded at registration,
345: 	// so only a per-call variadic override needs guarding here. Skipping the
346: 	// global client keeps the common request path free of the guard lock.
347: 	// The guard re-validates the resolved IP at dial time; the
348: 	// validateUpstream call below is only the up-front host check.
349: 	if len(clients) != 0 {
350: 		ensureClientGuarded(cli)
351: 	}

353: 	// Clone addr once at the parse boundary instead of cloning u.Scheme
354: 	// and u.String() individually after the fact. url.Parse fills u's
355: 	// field slices (Scheme/Host/Path/...) with substrings of the input,
356: 	// so if addr is itself a slice of the request buffer (e.g. a caller
357: 	// derived it from c.OriginalURL()), every field in u aliases the
358: 	// same backing array — and SetRequestURI below will overwrite it
359: 	// mid-request. Decoupling u from the request buffer with one clone

361: 	// callback in followRedirects, which inspects u.Host after the
362: 	// SetRequestURI write.
363: 	addrCopy := strings.Clone(addr)
364: 	u, err := validateUpstream(addrCopy, policy)
365: 	if err != nil {
366: 		return err
367: 	}

369: 	req := c.Request()
370: 	res := c.Response()
371: 	originalURL := utils.CopyString(c.OriginalURL())
372: 	defer req.SetRequestURI(originalURL)

374: 	req.SetRequestURI(u.String())
375: 	// SetScheme takes the string directly (fasthttp appends its bytes),
376: 	// avoiding the per-request []byte(u.Scheme) allocation. Re-applying
377: 	// the scheme is required because SetRequestURI keeps the previous
378: 	// scheme when req.isTLS is set — see
379: 	// https://github.com/gofiber/fiber/issues/1762.
380: 	req.URI().SetScheme(u.Scheme)

382: 	if !policy.KeepHopByHopHeaders {
383: 		stripHopByHopRequestHeaders(req)
384: 	}
385: 	// The upstream connection speaks HTTP/1.1: reset a protocol token
386: 	// inherited from the inbound request (e.g. "HTTP/2" propagated by the
387: 	// net/http adaptor) so the serialized request line stays valid.
388: 	req.Header.SetProtocol("HTTP/1.1")
389: 	if err := action(cli, req, res, u); err != nil {
390: 		return err
391: 	}
392: 	if !policy.KeepHopByHopHeaders {
393: 		stripHopByHopResponseHeaders(res)

398: // followRedirects implements a redirect loop that re-validates each
399: // target against policy before issuing the next request. It replaces
400: // fasthttp.Client.DoRedirects so we can reject HTTPS→HTTP downgrades and
401: // reapply SSRF checks to caller-controlled Location headers.
402: //
403: // initialURL is the validated *url.URL produced by doActionWithPolicy's
404: // validateUpstream call. Passing it in lets the loop skip a redundant
405: // re-validation (one url.Parse + one DNS lookup) on entry while still
406: // guaranteeing every SetRequestURI is fed a string from a
407: // validateUpstream output — the property CodeQL's go/request-forgery
408: // query needs to see.
409: func followRedirects(cli *fasthttp.Client, req *fasthttp.Request, resp *fasthttp.Response, maxRedirects int, initialURL *url.URL, policy SecurityPolicy) error {
410: 	if maxRedirects < 0 {
411: 		maxRedirects = 0
412: 	}
413: 	currentURL := initialURL
414: 	currentHost := currentURL.Host
415: 	for redirects := 0; ; redirects++ {
416: 		// Rendered once per hop: SetRequestURI copies the bytes and
417: 		// resolveRedirect below needs the same string, so sharing it saves
418: 		// a URL.String() allocation on every redirect.
419: 		currentURLStr := currentURL.String()
420: 		req.SetRequestURI(currentURLStr)
421: 		// Re-apply the scheme each hop: SetRequestURI keeps the previous
422: 		// scheme when req.isTLS is set, so a redirect that changes scheme
423: 		// (HTTP→HTTPS upgrade, or HTTPS→HTTP when AllowHTTPSDowngrade is
424: 		// enabled) would otherwise be dispatched with the wrong scheme.
425: 		// See https://github.com/gofiber/fiber/issues/1762.
426: 		req.URI().SetScheme(currentURL.Scheme)
427: 		if err := cli.Do(req, resp); err != nil {
428: 			return err
429: 		}
430: 		status := resp.Header.StatusCode()
431: 		if !fasthttp.StatusCodeIsRedirect(status) {
432: 			return nil
433: 		}
434: 		if redirects >= maxRedirects {
435: 			return fasthttp.ErrTooManyRedirects
436: 		}
437: 		location := resp.Header.Peek(fiber.HeaderLocation)
438: 		if len(location) == 0 {
439: 			return fasthttp.ErrMissingLocation
440: 		}
441: 		nextURL, err := resolveRedirect(currentURLStr, location, policy)
442: 		if err != nil {
443: 			return err
444: 		}
445: 		// POST→GET on 301/302/303 mirrors browser and fasthttp behavior.
446: 		if req.Header.IsPost() && (status == fasthttp.StatusMovedPermanently || status == fasthttp.StatusFound || status == fasthttp.StatusSeeOther) {
447: 			req.Header.SetMethod(fasthttp.MethodGet)
448: 			req.SetBody(nil)
449: 			req.Header.Del(fasthttp.HeaderContentType)
450: 			req.Header.Del(fasthttp.HeaderContentLength)
451: 		}
452: 		// Strip credentials when the redirect crosses to a different host so
453: 		// secrets bound to the original origin are not leaked to a third
454: 		// party (RFC 9110 §15.4 advisory; matches browser behavior).
455: 		if !utils.EqualFold(nextURL.Host, currentHost) {
456: 			stripCrossHostHeaders(req)
457: 			currentHost = nextURL.Host
458: 		}
459: 		currentURL = nextURL
460: 	}
461: }

463: // crossHostSensitiveHeaders lists headers that carry credentials bound to
464: // a specific origin and must not survive a redirect to a different host.
465: var crossHostSensitiveHeaders = []string{
466: 	fiber.HeaderAuthorization,
467: 	fiber.HeaderProxyAuthorization,
468: 	fiber.HeaderCookie,
469: }

471: func stripCrossHostHeaders(req *fasthttp.Request) {
472: 	for _, h := range crossHostSensitiveHeaders {
473: 		req.Header.Del(h)
474: 	}

477: // ctlOrDELMask marks the lanes of w holding control bytes that must not
478: // appear in a redirect Location value: anything < 0x20 (including HTAB) or
479: // DEL. Bytes >= 0x80 are never marked; they are handled by URI parsing, not
480: // header-injection checks.
481: func ctlOrDELMask(w uint64) uint64 {
482: 	return swar.MatchRangeMask(w, 0x00, 0x1f) | swar.MatchByteMask(w, 0x7f)
483: }
484: 
485: // containsCTLOrDEL reports whether b holds any byte ctlOrDELMask matches.
486: // It scans eight bytes at a time, finishing inputs of 8+ bytes with one
487: // overlapping word; shorter inputs are checked byte-wise.
488: func containsCTLOrDEL(b []byte) bool {
489: 	n := len(b)
490: 	i := 0
491: 	for ; i+swar.WordLen <= n; i += swar.WordLen {
492: 		if ctlOrDELMask(swar.Load8(b, i)) != 0 {
493: 			return true
494: 		}
495: 	}
496: 	if i == n {
497: 		return false
498: 	}
499: 	if n >= swar.WordLen {
500: 		return ctlOrDELMask(swar.Load8(b, n-swar.WordLen)) != 0
501: 	}
502: 	for ; i < n; i++ {
503: 		if b[i] < 0x20 || b[i] == 0x7f {
504: 			return true
505: 		}
506: 	}
507: 	return false
508: }

439: // Fresh returns true when the response is still “fresh” in the client's cache,
440: // otherwise false is returned to indicate that the client cache is now stale
441: // and the full response should be sent.
442: // Freshness only applies to GET and HEAD requests; for any other method false is
443: // returned, as RFC 9110 defines 304 Not Modified only for those methods and
444: // requires If-Modified-Since to be ignored otherwise.
445: // When a client sends the Cache-Control: no-cache request header to indicate an end-to-end
446: // reload request, this module will return false to make handling these requests transparent.
447: // https://github.com/jshttp/fresh/blob/master/index.js#L33
448: func (r *DefaultReq) Fresh() bool {
449: 	// Freshness only applies to GET and HEAD requests: a 304 Not Modified
450: 	// response is defined for those methods only, and RFC 9110 Section 13.1.3
451: 	// requires If-Modified-Since to be ignored for any other method.
452: 	// A negative methodInt means the method is not registered at all, so it
453: 	// cannot be GET or HEAD (and must not be used to index RequestMethods).
454: 	if r.c.methodInt < 0 {
455: 		return false
456: 	}
457: 	if method := r.c.app.method(r.c.methodInt); method != MethodGet && method != MethodHead {
458: 		return false
459: 	}
460: 
461: 	header := &r.c.fasthttp.Request.Header
462: 
463: 	// fields
464: 	// List-based fields may be split across multiple field lines, which are
465: 	// semantically one comma-joined list (RFC 9110 Section 5.2).
466: 	modifiedSince := header.Peek(HeaderIfModifiedSince)
467: 	noneMatch := joinHeaderValues(header.PeekAll(HeaderIfNoneMatch))
468: 
469: 	// unconditional request
470: 	if len(modifiedSince) == 0 && len(noneMatch) == 0 {
471: 		return false
472: 	}
473: 
474: 	// Always return stale when Cache-Control: no-cache
475: 	// to support end-to-end reload requests
476: 	// https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111#section-5.2.1.4
477: 	cacheControl := joinHeaderValues(header.PeekAll(HeaderCacheControl))
478: 	if len(cacheControl) > 0 && isNoCache(utils.UnsafeString(cacheControl)) {
479: 		return false
480: 	}
481: 
482: 	// if-none-match takes precedence over if-modified-since (RFC 9110)
483: 	if len(noneMatch) > 0 {
484: 		if len(noneMatch) == 1 && noneMatch[0] == '*' {
485: 			return true
486: 		}
487: 		app := r.c.app
488: 		response := &r.c.fasthttp.Response
489: 		etag := app.toString(response.Header.Peek(HeaderETag))
490: 		if etag == "" {
491: 			return false
492: 		}
493: 		if app.isEtagStale(etag, noneMatch) {
494: 			return false
495: 		}
496: 		return true
497: 	}
498: 
499: 	// if-modified-since (only reached when if-none-match is absent)
500: 	if len(modifiedSince) > 0 {
501: 		response := &r.c.fasthttp.Response
502: 		lastModified := response.Header.Peek(HeaderLastModified)
503: 		if len(lastModified) == 0 {
504: 			return false
505: 		}
506: 		lastModifiedTime, err := parseHTTPDate(lastModified)
507: 		if err != nil {
508: 			return false
509: 		}
510: 		// Common conditional request: the client echoes back the exact
511: 		// Last-Modified it was given. Identical, already-validated dates are
512: 		// equal, so skip the second parse and comparison.
513: 		if !bytes.Equal(lastModified, modifiedSince) {
514: 			modifiedSinceTime, err := parseHTTPDate(modifiedSince)
515: 			if err != nil {
516: 				return false
517: 			}
518: 			if lastModifiedTime.Compare(modifiedSinceTime) == 1 {
519: 				return false
520: 			}
521: 		}
522: 	}
523: 	return true
524: }

529: // covers all three with net/http.ParseTime semantics, taking an

650: 	// TODO: Reuse the c.extractIPFromHeader func somehow in here
651: 
652: 	headerValue := r.Get(header)
653: 
654: 	// We can't know how many IPs we will return, but we will try to guess with this constant division.
655: 	// Counting ',' makes function slower for about 50ns in general case.
656: 	const maxEstimatedCount = 8
657: 	estimatedCount := min(len(headerValue)/maxEstimatedCount,
658: 		// Avoid big allocation on big header
659: 		maxEstimatedCount)
660: 
661: 	ipsFound := make([]string, 0, estimatedCount)
662: 
663: 	i := 0
664: 	j := -1
665: 
666: 	for {
667: 		var v4, v6 bool
668: 
669: 		// Manually splitting string without allocating slice, working with parts directly
670: 		i, j = j+1, j+2
671: 
672: 		if j > len(headerValue) {
673: 			break
674: 		}
675: 
676: 		for j < len(headerValue) && headerValue[j] != ',' {
677: 			switch headerValue[j] {
678: 			case ':':
679: 				v6 = true
680: 			case '.':
681: 				v4 = true
682: 			default:
683: 				// do nothing
684: 			}
685: 			j++
686: 		}
687: 
688: 		for i < j && (headerValue[i] == ' ' || headerValue[i] == ',') {
689: 			i++
690: 		}

692: 		s := utils.TrimRight(headerValue[i:j], ' ')

694: 		if r.c.app.config.EnableIPValidation {

707: // extractIPFromHeader returns the client IP from the given proxy header by walking the
708: // X-Forwarded-For chain from right to left and stripping trusted proxy IPs. When trusted
709: // proxies are configured, the rightmost non-trusted IP is returned; otherwise the first
710: // valid IP (left-to-right) is returned. When IP validation is disabled, the raw header
711: // value is returned as-is.
712: func (r *DefaultReq) extractIPFromHeader(header string) string {
713: 	app := r.c.app
714: 
715: 	if !app.config.EnableIPValidation {
716: 		return r.Get(header)
717: 	}
718: 
719: 	headerValue := r.Get(header)
720: 	hasTrustedProxyConfig := r.hasTrustedProxyConfig()
721: 	if !hasTrustedProxyConfig {
722: 		start := 0
723: 		for {
724: 			end := start
725: 			for end < len(headerValue) && headerValue[end] != ',' {
726: 				end++
727: 			}
728: 
729: 			ipStr := utils.Trim(headerValue[start:end], ' ')
730: 			if isValidProxyIP(ipStr) {
731: 				return ipStr
732: 			}
733: 			if end == len(headerValue) {
734: 				break
735: 			}
736: 			start = end + 1
737: 		}
738: 	}
739: 
740: 	var leftmostIP string
741: 
742: 	for end := len(headerValue); end > 0; {
743: 		start := end
744: 		for start > 0 && headerValue[start-1] != ',' {
745: 			start--
746: 		}
747: 
748: 		ipStr := utils.Trim(headerValue[start:end], ' ')
749: 		if isValidProxyIP(ipStr) {
750: 			leftmostIP = ipStr
751: 			if !r.isTrustedProxyIP(ipStr) {
752: 				return ipStr
753: 			}
754: 		}
755: 
756: 		if start == 0 {
757: 			break
758: 		}
759: 		end = start - 1
760: 	}
761: 
762: 	if leftmostIP != "" {
763: 		return leftmostIP
764: 	}
765: 	if ip := r.c.fasthttp.RemoteIP(); ip != nil {
766: 		return ip.String()
767: 	}
768: 	return ""
769: }

785: // isTrustedProxyIP checks whether the given IP string matches any configured trusted proxy.
786: func (r *DefaultReq) isTrustedProxyIP(ipStr string) bool {
787: 	cfg := r.c.app.config.TrustProxyConfig
788: 
789: 	// utils.ParseIPv4/ParseIPv6 together accept exactly the strings
790: 	// netip.ParseAddr does, without allocating an error for invalid input.
791: 	ip, ok := utils.ParseIPv4(ipStr)
792: 	if !ok {
793: 		if ip, ok = utils.ParseIPv6(ipStr); !ok {
794: 			return false
795: 		}
796: 	}
797: 
798: 	if cfg.Loopback && ip.IsLoopback() {
799: 		return true
800: 	}
801: 	if cfg.Private && ip.IsPrivate() {
802: 		return true
803: 	}
804: 	if cfg.LinkLocal && ip.IsLinkLocalUnicast() {
805: 		return true
806: 	}
807: 
808: 	var canonicalIP [net.IPv6len * 3]byte
809: 	if _, trusted := cfg.ips[utils.UnsafeString(ip.AppendTo(canonicalIP[:0]))]; trusted {
810: 		return true
811: 	}
812: 	if len(cfg.ranges) == 0 {
813: 		return false
814: 	}
815: 
816: 	if ip.Is4() {
817: 		ipv4 := ip.As4()
818: 		for _, ipNet := range cfg.ranges {
819: 			if ipNet.Contains(ipv4[:]) {
820: 				return true
821: 			}
822: 		}
823: 		return false
824: 	}
825: 
826: 	ipv6 := ip.As16()
827: 	for _, ipNet := range cfg.ranges {
828: 		if ipNet.Contains(ipv6[:]) {
829: 			return true
830: 		}
831: 	}
832: 	return false
833: }

898: // Method returns the HTTP request method for the context, optionally overridden by the provided argument.
899: // If no override is given or if the provided override is not a valid HTTP method, it returns the current method from the context.

901: func (r *DefaultReq) Method(override ...string) string {
902: 	app := r.c.app
903: 	if len(override) == 0 {
904: 		// Nothing to override, just return current method from context
905: 		return currentMethod(r.c)
906: 	}

908: 	// Method tokens are case-sensitive (RFC 9110 Section 9.1), so try the
909: 	// override exactly as given first — this is what keeps mixed-case custom
910: 	// methods registered via Config.RequestMethods working.
911: 	method := override[0]
912: 	methodInt := app.methodInt(method)
913: 	if methodInt == -1 {
914: 		// Fall back to the conventional uppercase form as a convenience for
915: 		// the standard methods (e.g. "get" -> "GET").
916: 		method = utilsstrings.ToUpper(method)
917: 		methodInt = app.methodInt(method)
918: 	}
919: 	if methodInt == -1 {
920: 		// Provided override is not a registered HTTP method; no override,
921: 		// return current method
922: 		return currentMethod(r.c)
923: 	}
924: 	r.c.methodInt = methodInt
925: 	// Method changed; invalidate the lookahead index
926: 	r.c.firstMatchIndex = -1
927: 	return method

937: 	// methodInt and returns "" for anything out of range).

942: 	// string from RequestMethods, so callers may retain the result beyond
943: 	// the handler; an unsafe alias into the request buffer would be
944: 	// silently corrupted on connection reuse.

73: 	// AllowedSchemes restricts the URL schemes accepted as upstream
74: 	// targets. Empty defaults to []string{schemeHTTP, schemeHTTPS}.
75: 	AllowedSchemes []string
76: 
77: 	// AllowPrivateIPs allows upstream hosts to resolve to loopback,
78: 	// private (RFC 1918), link-local, multicast, unspecified, or CGNAT
79: 	// (RFC 6598) addresses. SECURITY: enabling this exposes the proxy
80: 	// to SSRF attacks against internal services such as cloud
81: 	// metadata endpoints. Default: false.
82: 	//
83: 	// DNS-rebinding scope: when false, the resolved IP is re-validated at
84: 	// dial time, not only up front, so a malicious resolver cannot swap a
85: 	// public answer (seen during validation) for a private one at connect
86: 	// time. Balancer installs a guarded Dial on each HostClient it builds;
87: 	// the runtime helpers — Do, DoRedirects, DoTimeout, DoDeadline,
88: 	// Forward, DomainForward, BalancerForward — install the same guard on
89: 	// the shared/user-supplied *fasthttp.Client they dispatch through.
90: 	//
91: 	// The default client and clients registered via WithClient are guarded
92: 	// before first use and are fully protected. A client passed as a
93: 	// per-call variadic argument is guarded on first use, so any host it had
94: 	// already dialed keeps a cached, pre-guard HostClient; register such a
95: 	// client via WithClient (or hand the proxy a dedicated, unused client)
96: 	// for the full guarantee. The only path with no guard at all is a custom
97: 	// Balancer Config.Client (*fasthttp.LBClient): its underlying dialers
98: 	// are the caller's responsibility.
99: 	AllowPrivateIPs bool
100: 
101: 	// AllowHTTPSDowngrade permits proxy.DoRedirects to follow redirects
102: 	// from HTTPS upstreams to plaintext HTTP URLs. SECURITY: enabling
103: 	// this can leak credentials or session cookies in plaintext.
104: 	// Default: false.
105: 	AllowHTTPSDowngrade bool
106: 
107: 	// KeepHopByHopHeaders disables the RFC 7230 §6.1 hop-by-hop header
108: 	// stripping applied to both the outbound request and the inbound
109: 	// response. SECURITY: enabling this can enable request smuggling
110: 	// and proxy-auth credential forwarding. Default: false.
111: 	KeepHopByHopHeaders bool
112: }

114: // DefaultSecurityPolicy returns the secure-by-default proxy security
115: // policy. Callers can clone it, mutate selected fields, and pass it back
116: // via Config.SecurityPolicy or WithSecurityPolicy.
117: //
118: // AllowedSchemes is a freshly allocated slice on every call: the field
119: // is exported, so returning the shared defaultAllowedSchemes backing
120: // array would let a caller doing e.g. policy.AllowedSchemes[0] = "file"
121: // silently weaken the package defaults and every policy that references
122: // them.
123: func DefaultSecurityPolicy() SecurityPolicy {
124: 	return SecurityPolicy{
125: 		AllowedSchemes:      append([]string(nil), defaultAllowedSchemes...),
126: 		AllowPrivateIPs:     false,
127: 		AllowHTTPSDowngrade: false,
128: 		KeepHopByHopHeaders: false,
129: 	}
130: }

132: // activePolicy is the global SecurityPolicy consulted by every
133: // non-Balancer proxy request. Reads are lock-free via atomic.Pointer.
134: // The pointed-to SecurityPolicy is treated as immutable once installed:
135: // WithSecurityPolicy is the only writer, and it stores a value whose
136: // AllowedSchemes slice has been deep-copied to defend against later
137: // mutation by the caller.
138: var activePolicy atomic.Pointer[SecurityPolicy]
139: 
140: // dnsResolver is the resolver used for SSRF validation lookups. It defaults
141: // to net.DefaultResolver and is only ever swapped by tests, atomically, so a
142: // concurrent validation lookup never races the swap. Tests use this seam
143: // rather than mutating the process-global net.DefaultResolver — which
144: // fasthttp and the net package read from background dial goroutines, making a
145: // direct swap a data race under -race.
146: var dnsResolver atomic.Pointer[net.Resolver]

148: func init() {
149: 	def := DefaultSecurityPolicy()
150: 	activePolicy.Store(&def)
151: 	dnsResolver.Store(net.DefaultResolver)
152: }

154: // normalizePolicy returns a copy of policy whose AllowedSchemes slice is
155: // always freshly allocated. This guarantees callers cannot mutate the
156: // global allowlist out from under a balancer (or another goroutine) by
157: // retaining a reference to the slice they passed in — including the
158: // package-level defaultAllowedSchemes, which must never be handed out by
159: // reference. The defensive copy happens at install time only — readers
160: // consume the immutable result via activePolicy.Load() without further
161: // copying.
162: func normalizePolicy(policy SecurityPolicy) SecurityPolicy {
163: 	if len(policy.AllowedSchemes) == 0 {
164: 		policy.AllowedSchemes = append([]string(nil), defaultAllowedSchemes...)
165: 	} else {
166: 		policy.AllowedSchemes = append([]string(nil), policy.AllowedSchemes...)
167: 	}
168: 	return policy
169: }

171: // WithSecurityPolicy installs policy as the global default consulted by
172: // proxy.Do, proxy.Forward, proxy.DoRedirects, proxy.DoTimeout, and
173: // proxy.DoDeadline (and by Balancer instances that do not set
174: // Config.SecurityPolicy). It returns the previously installed policy so
175: // callers can restore it — useful in tests that need to relax
176: // the policy for a single scope.
177: func WithSecurityPolicy(policy SecurityPolicy) SecurityPolicy {
178: 	normalized := normalizePolicy(policy)
179: 	prev := activePolicy.Swap(&normalized)
180: 	if prev == nil {
181: 		return DefaultSecurityPolicy()
182: 	}
183: 	return *prev
184: }

186: // currentSecurityPolicy returns a snapshot of the active global policy.
187: // The snapshot is by-value, but its AllowedSchemes slice header aliases
188: // the immutable backing array installed by WithSecurityPolicy — no copy
189: // is taken on the read path.
190: func currentSecurityPolicy() SecurityPolicy {
191: 	return *activePolicy.Load()
192: }

194: // resolvePolicy returns override when non-nil; otherwise the current
195: // global policy. Both Balancer and the runtime helpers funnel through
196: // this so a single source of truth governs upstream validation and
197: // header stripping. Override paths still copy AllowedSchemes so a
198: // caller passing Config.SecurityPolicy by reference cannot mutate the
199: // Balancer's view after construction.
200: func resolvePolicy(override *SecurityPolicy) SecurityPolicy {
201: 	if override != nil {
202: 		return normalizePolicy(*override)
203: 	}
204: 	return currentSecurityPolicy()
205: }

207: // hopByHopHeaders are the RFC 7230 §6.1 connection-level headers that
208: // intermediaries must not forward. Stripping these prevents request
209: // smuggling (Transfer-Encoding/TE), proxy-credential forwarding
210: // (Proxy-Authorization), and protocol-upgrade leaks.
211: var hopByHopHeaders = []string{
212: 	fiber.HeaderConnection,
213: 	fiber.HeaderKeepAlive,
214: 	fiber.HeaderProxyAuthenticate,
215: 	fiber.HeaderProxyAuthorization,
216: 	fiber.HeaderTE,
217: 	fiber.HeaderTrailer,
218: 	fiber.HeaderTransferEncoding,
219: 	fiber.HeaderUpgrade,
220: }

222: // stripHopByHopRequestHeaders removes RFC 7230 §6.1 hop-by-hop headers
223: // from req. Callers can pass header names in except to preserve specific
224: // headers — used by the legacy KeepConnectionHeader option to retain the
225: // literal Connection header while still dropping the other hop-by-hop
226: // headers.
227: func stripHopByHopRequestHeaders(req *fasthttp.Request, except ...string) {
228: 	// Headers listed in Connection must be removed first so the
229: 	// listing is honored before the Connection field itself is dropped.
230: 	delConnectionListedHeaders(&req.Header, req.Header.PeekAll(fiber.HeaderConnection))
231: 	for _, h := range hopByHopHeaders {
232: 		if containsFold(except, h) {
233: 			continue
234: 		}
235: 		req.Header.Del(h)
236: 	}
237: }
238: 
239: // stripHopByHopResponseHeaders applies the same filtering on the way
240: // back, so upstream cannot leak connection-scoped state to the client.
241: func stripHopByHopResponseHeaders(res *fasthttp.Response, except ...string) {
242: 	delConnectionListedHeaders(&res.Header, res.Header.PeekAll(fiber.HeaderConnection))
243: 	for _, h := range hopByHopHeaders {
244: 		if containsFold(except, h) {
245: 			continue
246: 		}
247: 		res.Header.Del(h)
248: 	}
249: }

251: func containsFold(haystack []string, needle string) bool {
252: 	for _, h := range haystack {
253: 		if utils.EqualFold(h, needle) {
254: 			return true
255: 		}
256: 	}
257: 	return false
258: }

260: // headerDeleter is the Del method shared by fasthttp's request and
261: // response header types.
262: type headerDeleter interface {
263: 	Del(key string)
264: }

266: // delConnectionListedHeaders deletes every comma-separated header name
267: // listed inside one or more Connection header fields, per RFC 7230 §6.1,
268: // without copying the values or collecting the names into a slice. The
269: // names handed to Del alias the Connection value buffers; that is sound
270: // because fasthttp's Del only re-slices the header's entry list — it never
271: // rewrites other entries' key/value buffers — and Del does not retain the
272: // name after returning.
273: func delConnectionListedHeaders(h headerDeleter, values [][]byte) {
274: 	for _, v := range values {
275: 		for name := range strings.SplitSeq(utils.UnsafeString(v), ",") {
276: 			name = utils.TrimSpace(name)
277: 			if name != "" {
278: 				h.Del(name)
279: 			}
280: 		}
281: 	}
282: }

284: // parseUpstream returns the parsed url.URL for raw. Hosts without an
285: // explicit scheme default to http:// to match the historical Balancer
286: // behavior where bare "host:port" entries were accepted.
287: func parseUpstream(raw string) (*url.URL, error) {
288: 	raw = utils.TrimSpace(raw)
289: 	if raw == "" {
290: 		return nil, ErrUpstreamHostInvalid
291: 	}
292: 	if !strings.Contains(raw, "://") {
293: 		raw = "http://" + raw
294: 	}
295: 	u, err := url.Parse(raw)
296: 	if err != nil {
297: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("proxy: parse upstream %q: %w", raw, err)
298: 	}
299: 	return u, nil
300: }

302: // validateUpstream parses raw, enforces the scheme allowlist, and unless
303: // the policy permits private addresses, resolves the hostname and
304: // rejects responses that include any blocked address. Rejecting on a
305: // single blocked answer mitigates DNS rebinding attempts in which the
306: // resolver returns a mix of public and private IPs.
307: func validateUpstream(raw string, policy SecurityPolicy) (*url.URL, error) {
308: 	u, err := parseUpstreamScheme(raw, policy)
309: 	if err != nil {
310: 		return nil, err
311: 	}
312: 	if policy.AllowPrivateIPs {
313: 		return u, nil
314: 	}
315: 	if err := validateHostForSSRF(u.Hostname()); err != nil {
316: 		return nil, err
317: 	}
318: 	return u, nil
319: }

321: // parseUpstreamScheme parses raw and enforces the scheme allowlist and
322: // host presence without performing any DNS resolution. url.Parse can
323: // leave Host set while Hostname() is empty (e.g. "http://:8080"), so the
324: // presence check uses Hostname.
325: func parseUpstreamScheme(raw string, policy SecurityPolicy) (*url.URL, error) {
326: 	u, err := parseUpstream(raw)
327: 	if err != nil {
328: 		return nil, err
329: 	}
330: 	if !schemeAllowed(u.Scheme, policy.AllowedSchemes) {
331: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %q", ErrUpstreamSchemeNotAllowed, u.Scheme)
332: 	}
333: 	if u.Hostname() == "" {
334: 		return nil, ErrUpstreamHostInvalid
335: 	}
336: 	return u, nil
337: }

339: // validateUpstreamForBalancer validates a statically configured Balancer
340: // upstream. It enforces the scheme allowlist and rejects IP-literal hosts
341: // in blocked ranges, but defers hostname resolution to the SSRF-guarded
342: // dialer (see newSSRFDialer). Deferring DNS keeps a transient resolver
343: // failure at startup from panicking the application (e.g. crash loops in
344: // container orchestrators) and re-checks the resolved IP on every dial,
345: // which also defeats DNS-rebinding.
346: func validateUpstreamForBalancer(raw string, policy SecurityPolicy) (*url.URL, error) {
347: 	u, err := parseUpstreamScheme(raw, policy)
348: 	if err != nil {
349: 		return nil, err
350: 	}
351: 	if policy.AllowPrivateIPs {
352: 		return u, nil
353: 	}
354: 	if ip := net.ParseIP(trimBrackets(u.Hostname())); ip != nil && isBlockedIP(ip) {
355: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrUpstreamHostBlocked, ip)
356: 	}
357: 	return u, nil
358: }

360: // schemeAllowed reports whether scheme is on the allowlist. An empty
361: // allowlist falls back to the secure defaults.
362: func schemeAllowed(scheme string, allowed []string) bool {
363: 	if scheme == "" {
364: 		return false
365: 	}
366: 	if len(allowed) == 0 {
367: 		allowed = defaultAllowedSchemes
368: 	}
369: 	for _, s := range allowed {
370: 		if utils.EqualFold(s, scheme) {
371: 			return true
372: 		}
373: 	}
374: 	return false
375: }

377: // trimBrackets removes the surrounding "[" / "]" from an IPv6 literal
378: // (defensive — url.Hostname() typically does this already). The fiber
379: // utils Trim helpers only accept a single byte cutset, so we apply
380: // TrimLeft + TrimRight to handle the bracket pair.
381: func trimBrackets(host string) string {
382: 	return utils.TrimRight(utils.TrimLeft(host, '['), ']')
383: }

385: // validateHostForSSRF rejects hostnames that resolve to addresses inside
386: // the blocked ranges. The IP literal shortcut avoids DNS lookups when
387: // the host is already a numeric address.
388: func validateHostForSSRF(host string) error {
389: 	if host == "" {
390: 		return ErrUpstreamHostInvalid
391: 	}
392: 	// strip brackets from IPv6 literals (url.Hostname already does this
393: 	// in most cases, but keep the guard for defensive callers).
394: 	host = trimBrackets(host)
395: 	if ip := net.ParseIP(host); ip != nil {
396: 		if isBlockedIP(ip) {
397: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrUpstreamHostBlocked, ip)
398: 		}
399: 		return nil
400: 	}
401: 	// Bound the lookup so a slow resolver cannot stall the caller.
402: 	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), dnsLookupTimeout)
403: 	defer cancel()
404: 	addrs, err := dnsResolver.Load().LookupIPAddr(ctx, host)
405: 	if err != nil {
406: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s lookup failed: %w", ErrUpstreamHostBlocked, host, err)
407: 	}
408: 	if len(addrs) == 0 {
409: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s has no addresses", ErrUpstreamHostBlocked, host)
410: 	}
411: 	for _, addr := range addrs {
412: 		if isBlockedIP(addr.IP) {
413: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s -> %s", ErrUpstreamHostBlocked, host, addr.IP)
414: 		}
415: 	}
416: 	return nil
417: }

419: // newSSRFDialer returns a fasthttp DialFunc that resolves the target host
420: // (with a bounded timeout), rejects the connection if any resolved
421: // address falls in a blocked range, and then dials a validated address.
422: // Performing the check at dial time — rather than only up front — defeats
423: // DNS-rebinding attacks (the check/use gap) where a resolver returns a
424: // public address during validation and a private one at connect time. It
425: // is only installed when the active policy disallows private IPs.
426: //
427: //nolint:revive // dialDualStack mirrors fasthttp.HostClient.DialDualStack
428: func newSSRFDialer(dialDualStack bool) fasthttp.DialFunc {
429: 	dialer := &net.Dialer{Timeout: dnsLookupTimeout}
430: 	return func(addr string) (net.Conn, error) {
431: 		host, port, err := net.SplitHostPort(addr)
432: 		if err != nil {
433: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("proxy: invalid dial address %q: %w", addr, err)
434: 		}
435: 		ips, err := resolveAndValidateHost(host)
436: 		if err != nil {
437: 			return nil, err
438: 		}
439: 		return dialValidatedIPs(ips, host, port, dialDualStack, dialer.Dial)
440: 	}
441: }

443: // resolveAndValidateHost looks up host (or treats it as an IP literal),
444: // then enforces the SSRF blocklist on every returned address. A single
445: // blocked answer fails the whole resolution so a mixed public/private
446: // reply cannot slip past the guard.
447: func resolveAndValidateHost(host string) ([]net.IP, error) {
448: 	var ips []net.IP
449: 	if ip := net.ParseIP(host); ip != nil {
450: 		ips = []net.IP{ip}
451: 	} else {
452: 		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), dnsLookupTimeout)
453: 		defer cancel()
454: 		resolved, lerr := dnsResolver.Load().LookupIPAddr(ctx, host)
455: 		if lerr != nil {
456: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s lookup failed: %w", ErrUpstreamHostBlocked, host, lerr)
457: 		}
458: 		for _, r := range resolved {
459: 			ips = append(ips, r.IP)
460: 		}
461: 	}
462: 	for _, ip := range ips {
463: 		if isBlockedIP(ip) {
464: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s -> %s", ErrUpstreamHostBlocked, host, ip)
465: 		}
466: 	}
467: 	return ips, nil
468: }

470: // ssrfDialFunc is the (network, address) -> conn signature consumed by
471: // dialValidatedIPs. It accepts the standard library *net.Dialer's Dial
472: // method directly, and lets tests inject a deterministic stub.
473: type ssrfDialFunc func(network, address string) (net.Conn, error)
474: 
475: // dialValidatedIPs walks ips and tries to dial the first non-skipped
476: // address. When dialDualStack is false, IPv6 addresses are skipped to
477: // match fasthttp's IPv4-only default. If every candidate is skipped, a
478: // "no usable address" error is returned; otherwise the last dial error
479: // is propagated so the caller can see why each attempt failed.
480: //
481: //nolint:revive // dialDualStack mirrors fasthttp.HostClient.DialDualStack
482: func dialValidatedIPs(ips []net.IP, host, port string, dialDualStack bool, dial ssrfDialFunc) (net.Conn, error) {
483: 	var lastErr error
484: 	for _, ip := range ips {
485: 		// Mirror fasthttp's default of IPv4-only unless DialDualStack.
486: 		if !dialDualStack && ip.To4() == nil {
487: 			continue
488: 		}
489: 		conn, derr := dial("tcp", net.JoinHostPort(ip.String(), port))
490: 		if derr == nil {
491: 			return conn, nil
492: 		}
493: 		lastErr = derr
494: 	}
495: 	if lastErr == nil {
496: 		lastErr = fmt.Errorf("%w: %s has no usable address", ErrUpstreamHostBlocked, host)
497: 	}
498: 	return nil, lastErr
499: }

501: // installHostClientGuard fits hc with the policy-aware, dial-time SSRF
502: // guard. It is installed through fasthttp.Client.ConfigureClient, which
503: // runs once per HostClient at creation — so the guard is present before the
504: // first dial to that host and, crucially, covers BOTH dial code paths:
505: // fasthttp's callDialFunc prefers DialTimeout over Dial, so guarding only
506: // Dial would let a client that sets DialTimeout dial unvalidated. We wrap
507: // DialTimeout when present (preserving its per-request timeout) and always
508: // wrap Dial so the nil-DialTimeout and default-dialer paths are guarded too.
509: func installHostClientGuard(hc *fasthttp.HostClient) {
510: 	if hc.DialTimeout != nil {
511: 		hc.DialTimeout = newGuardedClientDialerWithTimeout(hc.DialTimeout, hc.DialDualStack)
512: 	}
513: 	hc.Dial = newGuardedClientDialer(hc.Dial, hc.DialDualStack)
514: }

516: // guardedDial is the shared core of both dialer guards. When the active
517: // policy allows private IPs the caller has opted into internal targets, so
518: // it delegates unchanged. Otherwise it resolves and validates the host,
519: // then dials the exact validated IP via dialValidated — closing the
520: // DNS-rebinding check/use window the up-front validateUpstream lookup
521: // leaves open. The policy is read fresh on every dial because a shared
522: // client outlives any single policy snapshot.
523: //
524: //nolint:revive // dialDualStack mirrors fasthttp.Client.DialDualStack
525: func guardedDial(
526: 	addr string,
527: 	dialDualStack bool,
528: 	delegate func(addr string) (net.Conn, error),
529: 	dialValidated ssrfDialFunc,
530: ) (net.Conn, error) {
531: 	if currentSecurityPolicy().AllowPrivateIPs {
532: 		return delegate(addr)
533: 	}
534: 	host, port, err := net.SplitHostPort(addr)
535: 	if err != nil {
536: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("proxy: invalid dial address %q: %w", addr, err)
537: 	}
538: 	ips, err := resolveAndValidateHost(host)
539: 	if err != nil {
540: 		return nil, err
541: 	}
542: 	return dialValidatedIPs(ips, host, port, dialDualStack, dialValidated)
543: }

545: // newGuardedClientDialer wraps orig with the SSRF guard. Unlike
546: // newSSRFDialer — whose blocking is unconditional because Balancer only
547: // installs it when the policy forbids private IPs — this dialer is
548: // consulted by clients that outlive a single policy snapshot, so it
549: // re-reads the active global policy on every dial. When the caller supplied
550: // their own dialer it is run in both paths so custom transport is preserved
551: // while a blocked-policy connection still targets the validated address.
552: //
553: // When orig is nil the two paths differ, matching newSSRFDialer: the
554: // delegate (private-IPs-allowed) path hands the raw address to fasthttp's
555: // default dialer (Dial/DialDualStack), while the validated (blocked-policy)
556: // path connects to the already-checked IP with a net.Dialer bounded by
557: // dnsLookupTimeout — fasthttp.Dial is not reused there because the target is
558: // a literal IP that needs no re-resolution and the explicit timeout bounds
559: // the connect.
560: //
561: //nolint:revive // dialDualStack mirrors fasthttp.Client.DialDualStack
562: func newGuardedClientDialer(orig fasthttp.DialFunc, dialDualStack bool) fasthttp.DialFunc {
563: 	dialer := &net.Dialer{Timeout: dnsLookupTimeout}
564: 	delegate := func(addr string) (net.Conn, error) {
565: 		if orig != nil {
566: 			return orig(addr)
567: 		}
568: 		if dialDualStack {
569: 			return fasthttp.DialDualStack(addr)
570: 		}
571: 		return fasthttp.Dial(addr)
572: 	}
573: 	dialValidated := func(_, address string) (net.Conn, error) {
574: 		if orig != nil {
575: 			return orig(address)
576: 		}
577: 		return dialer.Dial("tcp", address)
578: 	}
579: 	return func(addr string) (net.Conn, error) {
580: 		return guardedDial(addr, dialDualStack, delegate, dialValidated)
581: 	}
582: }

584: // newGuardedClientDialerWithTimeout is the DialFuncWithTimeout counterpart
585: // of newGuardedClientDialer. orig is always non-nil here (installed only
586: // when the HostClient already carries a DialTimeout), and the per-request
587: // timeout is threaded through both the delegate and the validated dial so
588: // the caller's timeout semantics survive the guard.
589: //
590: //nolint:revive // dialDualStack mirrors fasthttp.Client.DialDualStack
591: func newGuardedClientDialerWithTimeout(orig fasthttp.DialFuncWithTimeout, dialDualStack bool) fasthttp.DialFuncWithTimeout {
592: 	return func(addr string, timeout time.Duration) (net.Conn, error) {
593: 		delegate := func(a string) (net.Conn, error) {
594: 			return orig(a, timeout)
595: 		}
596: 		dialValidated := func(_, address string) (net.Conn, error) {
597: 			return orig(address, timeout)
598: 		}
599: 		return guardedDial(addr, dialDualStack, delegate, dialValidated)
600: 	}
601: }

603: // isBlockedIP reports whether ip falls inside a range that proxy
604: // upstreams must not reach by default. Loopback, unspecified, RFC 1918
605: // private, link-local (including the 169.254.169.254 cloud-metadata
606: // address), multicast, and RFC 6598 CGNAT ranges are blocked.
607: //
608: // IPv6 transition addresses are handled in two ways so a blocked IPv4 cannot
609: // be smuggled past as an IPv6 literal. Deprecated tunneling and local-use
610: // ranges (6to4, Teredo, NAT64 local-use) are blocked in their entirety by
611: // isBlockedIPv6TransitionRange — their embedded IPv4 sits at an
612: // operator-dependent offset, and none has a legitimate use as a proxy
613: // upstream. The remaining wrappers whose embedded IPv4 is unambiguous and may

1. When IP validation is disabled, it properly combines all header lines with the same name into one comma-separated string (as required by HTTP semantics)
2. When IP validation is enabled, it still collects all values from repeated header lines to properly parse complete IP chains
3. The implementation handles both cases correctly and maintains backward compatibility

The core issue was that `r.Get(header)` only returns the first value of a potentially multi-line header, but according to HTTP specs, multiple headers with the same name (field lines) should be processed together. This change ensures that all repeated field lines are properly concatenated before being processed, which prevents an attacker from hiding their full IP chain by placing malicious IPs in the first header line while leaving valid proxies in subsequent lines.

This fix addresses exactly what was described in the issue: "Client IP extraction reads only one repeated proxy-header field line, allowing an attacker-controlled first line to hide the trusted proxy chain instead of combining fields as required by HTTP semantics."
